text:
For my hotel at night a sky rises

from the estuary slowly.

A bog of stars burns and this plaza

solitary, remains in

silence.

Without the sleepless lights of the tram,

without its yellow fruit and its clamor,

the steep streets fall asleep,

empty of children, and the shops

and liquor stores begin to close.

The hill is gentle and the greens are

a ruined estate, some palms,

a sad and certain colonial air,

witnesses that the Tagus reaches the

sea

and black ships with light bulbs reach the port.

Its siren is hoarse

like smoke!

Beautiful animals of the night,

funeral carriages

upon the water!

Old cities where there is always someone leaning out

over the balcony and the windows.

If I could be at that height,

I would look in silence and last forever:

all the blue, the river, and memory.

Down this street, there where I cannot reach

to see, my hotel,

the end where I look at myself

and another, in my place, leaves my name in a name

of another city and another river.


From "" 1991

translation.title: A Window onto the World
translation.editorial_note: The source’s “lentaniente” is corrected to the evident “lentamente” (“slowly”); the empty collection title in the supplied footer is retained as “From "" 1991” rather than invented.
